 Order
The order passed in Na.Ka.No.2237 of 2009/r/g/dated 28.06.2010 by the first respondent and the consequential order of the second respondent dated 10.01.2019 are under challenge.
2. The petitioner viz., K.Matheswaran submits that he was working as Secretary in the second respondent Bank.
The second respondent Bank issued a charge memo dated 30.09.2008 stating that he misappropriated Rs.42,000/-, from repyament of the loan amount of Rs.50,000/- belonging to one Ganesan.

The petitioner has become not eligible to work in the Co- operative Society under Section 162 of the Tamil Nadu Co-operative Societies Act, 1983, since he was sentenced to two years of imprisonment by the Judicial Magistrate No.II, Mettur in C.C.No.145/2004 by its Judgment dated 05.05.2005.
_ _ _ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 3
. The petitioner would further submit that he abstained from duty from 04.07.2005 without any permission.
He submitted an explanation to the second respondent dated 03.11.2008 and it was not considered by the second respondent and ordered for domestic enquiry on 04.11.2008.
After due enquiry, he was dismissed from service by order dated 10.01.2009.

Against the order of the dismissal dated 10.01.2009, the petitioner filed a revision petition before the first respondent under Section 153 of the Tamil Nadu Co-operative Societies Act, 1983 and it was also dismissed,
confirming the order of the second respondent.

4. The petitioner further submits that against the Judgment of the conviction passed in C.C.No.145/2004 dated 05.05/2005, the petitioner has preferred an appeal in C.A.No.8 of 2005 before the Additional District Court No.II, Salem and the Criminal Appeal was also dismissed.
5. Thereafter, the petitioner filed Criminal Revision Case in Crl.R.C.No.1481/2008 before this Court,
wherein, by Judgment dated 01.0.2011, the criminal revision case was allowed by setting aside the Judgment of the conviction and sentence passed by the Trial Court.
_ _ _ _ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 6.

Heard Mr.K.Selvaraj, learned counsel appearing for the petitioner, Mr.G.Krishnaraj, learned Additional Government Pleader appearing for the 1st respondent and Mr.L.P.Shanmuga Sundaram,
learned counsel appearing for the 2nd respondent.
7.

The learned counsel appearing for the petitioner contended that since the petitioner was acquitted from the criminal charges by this Court in Crl.R.C.No.1481/2008, the petitioner is entitled to be K.Madheswaran vs The Joint Registrar Of Co-Operative ...

As regards the charges that the petitioner abstained from duty dated 04.07.2005, the petitioner had submitted leave letter dated 04.07.2005 and 03.07.2006 to the second respondent Bank and the same was acknowledged by the second respondent Bank.

8. Mr.L.P.Shanmugasundaram, learned counsel for the second respondent strenuously contended that when he was working as Secretary of the Society and as per the complaint, the petitioner has misappropriated the deposit of the members by name, Ganesan to an extent of Rs.42,000/- and in that connection he was convicted by the Trial court and the said conviction was confirmed by the Appellate Court also in C.A.No.8/2005 by the Second Additional District Court, Salem.

He would also further contend ____________ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis that as he was absent and not reported duty which resulted in initiating disciplinary proceedings and after detailed enquiry, he was dismissed from service by an order dated 10.01.2019.
The petitioner now seeks for redressal which is sustainable in law.

9. From a careful perusal of the impugned order dated 10.01.2019, the petitioner was charged for the following two counts:-
i) Based on the deposit receipt of one Ganesan for an amount of Rs.42,000/-
without issuing such loan, the petitioner misappropriated the said amount and based upon the above, a case was registered by a Salem District Crime Branch Police, he was imposed to two years conviction.
ii) On 04.07.2005 onwards without applying leave, he abstained from duty.
10. The Trial Court convicted the petitioner and sentenced him to undergo two years Simple Imprisonment in C.C.No.145/2011 by its Judgment dated 05.05.2005.
The said Judgment was confirmed by the II Additional District Court, Salem, in an appeal preferred by the petitioner in C.A.No.8/2005.
Thereafter, the petitioner filed a criminal revision petition in Crl.R.C.No.1485/2008 before this Court.
By an order dated 01.02.2011, this Court allowed the criminal revision case.
____________ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 11.

For proper appreciation and understanding, the operative portion of the Judgment of this Court in Crl.R.C.No.1485 of 2008 is extracted hereunder:-
''7.

The entire reading of the judgment of the trial court would reveal that there is absolutely no reference about the evidence of D.W.1 and Exs.D1 and D3 documents particularly Ex.D3 report to the effect that the loan is obtained from the bank by the defacto complainant on his own and he lent the money to the first accused for interest.
Though the appellate court has referred to the evidence adduced on the side of the defence, it concluded as if the same does not disclose any ground to exonerate the accused from the charges.

Such finding is given without any detailed discussion K.Madheswaran vs The Joint Registrar Of Co-Operative ... on 12 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/70405385/
3 as to how the appellate court finds the same not supported the defence raised by the accused.

sentences.text: I am of the considered view that the failure on the part of the courts below to consider the prosecution case in the light of the admission made by the defacto complainant before the Sub Registrar upon enquiry made on his own complaint, as evidenced by the defence side evidence, resulted in an erroneous finding regarding the nature of the transaction and the manner in which the transaction is effected between the parties.

The very admission made by the defacto complainant before the enquiry officer by way of statement is sufficient enough to shatter the case of the prosecution regarding charges relating to act of cheating.
It may be true that the first accused did not repay the entire amount borrowed by him as and when demanded by the defacto complainant.
In that event, it is purely a civil dispute and the remedy available to P.W.1 is to approach appropriate civil forum for recovery of balance ____________ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis amount.

The conduct of P.W.1 in setting criminal law in motion, that too after admitting the nature of transaction before the Sub Registrar, amounts to abuse of process of law and the finding rendered by the courts below in the course of such proceeding is factually and legally unsustainable.

8.In the result, the criminal revision is allowed by setting aside the judgment of conviction and sentence dated 20.9.2006 made in C.A.No.8 of 2005 on the file of the Additional District Judge, (Fast Track Court No.II) Salem confirming the judgement dated 4.1.2005 made in C.C.No.145 of 2004 on the file of the Judicial Magistrate No.II, Mettur.

12. As regards, the Judgment of the conviction, it is ended in acquittal.

With regard to the second charge, the petitioner abstained from duty without leave application from 04.07.2005.
13.
The leaned counsel for the petitioner would contend that he had submitted a leave application on 04.07.2005.
But, the order dated 10.01.2019 passed by the second respondent reveals the fact that from 04.07.2005 onwards, he abstained from duty without following any rules.
However, it is relevant to note that the petitioner at the age of 56 years, filed ____________ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis this writ petition.
Now he is aged about 68 years and it is submitted that if at all his submission is positively taken into account he will be entitled to be paid salary upon Earned Leave and gratuity amount.
14. Based on the aforesaid discussions and in the circumstances, considering the age of the petitioner, the order of the first respondent is quashed in part.

As the petitioner is now 68 years old,
now he cannot be reinstated in service as sequel, the petitioner is entitled to be paid of Earned Leave salary and Gratuity amount.
The petitioner shall submit an requisition to that effect within a period of four weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.

On such requisition of the petitioner,
the 2nd respondent shall sanction the salary of Earned Leave and Gratuity amount, any other monetary benefits due payable by the respondents, within a period of eight weeks from the date of K.Madheswaran vs The Joint Registrar Of Co-Operative ...
